name: Distal Myopathy with Anterior Tibial Onset

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Distal Myopathy with Anterior Tibial Onset

criteria.description: Progressive weakness and atrophy predominantly affecting the anterior tibial muscles
Electromyography showing myopathic changes in distal lower limb muscles
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with distal myopathy (e.g., TTN, GNE mutations)
Muscle biopsy demonstrating myopathic features with rimmed vacuoles or fiber size variability
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive anterior tibial muscle weakness with myopathic EMG findings and genetic confirmation of pathogenic variant
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Muscle biopsy and family history support diagnosis but are not mandatory if genetic confirmation is present.

occasional.symptomName: Weakness of the intrinsic hand muscles

laboratory: Elevated serum creatine kinase (mild to moderate elevation)
imaging: Muscle MRI showing selective fatty replacement and atrophy of anterior tibial muscles
other: Muscle biopsy with rimmed vacuoles and fiber size variability

distinguishingFeatures: Predominant involvement of anterior tibial muscles without early distal hand involvement
Genetic mutations in TTN distinct from distal myopathy with anterior tibial onset
Early distal lower limb weakness with quadriceps sparing
Characteristic rimmed vacuoles on muscle biopsy

redFlags: Rapid progression of weakness over weeks
references: Udd B, et al. Distal myopathies. Handb Clin Neurol. 2011;101:113-127.
Orphanet: Distal myopathy with anterior tibial onset. ORPHA178400.
Haravuori H, et al. Distal myopathy with anterior tibial onset: clinical and genetic features. Neurology. 1998;50(1):123-130.
